old: When an encounter that contains one or more gravestones is *cleared*, the players may *scry* one card, however many gravestones the tile holds. The scry is resolved during Encounter Resolution, which states the cards that may be scried and what is done with them (see §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
new: When an encounter is *cleared*, the players may *scry* one card for each gravestone on its tile. Each scry is resolved during Encounter Resolution, which states the cards that may be scried and what is done with them (see §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
rationale: One scry for each gravestone: the token count is the rule, and the "however many" clause is deleted.
evidence: Official 2017 keys the benefit to each gravestone (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 755-759, 1385-1386); official 2022 lets each gravestone be used once (DS-TG 952-960).

old: 5. If the tile holds a *gravestone* {{icon:ast-0017-gravestone}}, the players may *scry* one card.
new: 5. The players may *scry* one card for each *gravestone* {{icon:ast-0017-gravestone}} on the tile.
rationale: Keeps the resolution step in line with §5.5.

old: When an encounter containing a gravestone is cleared, the players may scry one card of their collective choice (see §5.5, Gravestones). The card is one of the following.
new: When an encounter is cleared, the players may scry one card of their collective choice for each gravestone on its tile (see §5.5, Gravestones). The scries are resolved one at a time, and each card scried is one of the following.
rationale: Keeps the scry rule in line with §5.5 and fixes the order of several scries.

old: **Gravestone.** A terrain token or model. No model may *move*, *dodge*, or be pushed into a node containing a gravestone. When an encounter that contains a gravestone is *cleared*, the players may *scry* one card (see §5.5, Gravestones; §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
new: **Gravestone.** A terrain token or model. No model may *move*, *dodge*, or be pushed into a node containing a gravestone. When an encounter is *cleared*, the players may *scry* one card for each gravestone on its tile (see §5.5, Gravestones; §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
rationale: Glossary follows §5.5.

old: **Entry node.** A basic node adjacent to a doorway. When the characters enter a tile, they are placed on the entry nodes beside the doorway through which they entered (see §7.5, Encounter Start).
new: **Entry node.** A basic node along the tile edge that holds the doorway through which the characters entered the tile. When the characters enter a tile, they are placed on its entry nodes (see §7.5, Encounter Start).
rationale: A node cannot be adjacent to a doorway, which is not a node; the edge fixes which nodes are meant, and one definition serves §5.1, §7.5, §15.3 and the glossary.
evidence: Official 2017 example places the characters on any node along the edge of the doorway they entered by (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 415-422, 853-855).

old: **Entry node.** A basic node beside the doorway through which the characters entered the tile. Characters are placed on entry nodes at the start of an encounter, no more than three to a node. In a Level 4 encounter all four nodes along the wall beside the doorway are entry nodes (see §6.7).
new: **Entry node.** A basic node along the tile edge that holds the doorway through which the characters entered the tile. Characters are placed on entry nodes at the start of an encounter, no more than three to a node (see §5.1; §7.5, Encounter Start). In a Level 4 encounter the four basic nodes along that edge are the entry nodes (see §6.7).
rationale: Glossary follows §5.1.

old: **Basic node.** The most common node type. Basic nodes adjacent to a doorway are also entry nodes.
new: **Basic node.** The most common node type, printed in yellow. Trap tokens are dealt to basic nodes, and the basic nodes along the edge through which the characters entered a tile are its entry nodes (see §5.1).
rationale: Removes the second, looser definition of an entry node.

old: **Doorway.** A gap in a tile's wall through which characters pass between tiles. Basic nodes beside a doorway are entry nodes.
new: **Doorway.** A gap in a tile's wall through which the characters pass from one tile to the next. No model passes through a doorway during an encounter, and the basic nodes along the edge of the doorway by which the characters entered are the entry nodes (see §5.1; §5.2).
rationale: Removes the third, looser definition of an entry node and states the doorway rule of §5.2.

old: A spawn node or terrain node that holds no enemy or terrain is entered, left, and counted for range exactly as a basic node is.
new:
Tiles and encounter cards tell a primary spawn node from a secondary spawn node {{icon:ast-0010-secondary-spawn-node}}, and a primary terrain node from a secondary terrain node {{icon:ast-0018-secondary-terrain-node}}, by their icons. The difference shows which node receives which models or terrain and has no other effect.

A spawn node or terrain node that holds no enemy or terrain is entered, left, and counted for range exactly as a basic node is.
rationale: The encounter card cannot be read without knowing that the two icons name two different nodes.
evidence: Official 2017 symbol key lists primary and secondary spawn and terrain nodes (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 1830-1842).

old: The dodge follows every rule in §9.5, including the move that follows a successful dodge.
new: The dodge follows every rule in §9.5, including the movement that follows a successful dodge.
rationale: §5.2 states that the movement after a dodge is not a move; the noun is corrected.

old: A character targets enemies, bosses, and *invaders*.
new: A character targets hostile models: enemies, bosses, *invaders*, *mimics*, and *crystal lizards* (see §10.3).
rationale: §8.1 and §10.3 gave two different lists of what a character may target.

old: - The *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} shows the number of times the attack beside it is resolved (see §9.3).
new: - The *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} modifies no single icon: it shows the number of times the enemy's whole row of behaviour icons is resolved (see §9.1).
rationale: One meaning for the repeat icon on every data card and behaviour card: the whole row is repeated.
evidence: Official 2017: the enemy performs its entire behaviour (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 1441-1444); official 2022: entire row of behaviour symbols (DS-TG 2256-2264); this book, §16.1 step 4 and glossary Repeat.

old: A model is pushed for one of four reasons.
new: A model is pushed for one of the following reasons.
rationale: The list was not complete: a leap and other boss rules also push.

old: - A *boss* model moves onto the node of another boss model (see §17.1).
new:
- A *boss* model moves onto the node of another boss model (see §17.1).
- A rule of a boss pushes the model, as a *leap* does (see §16.2, Leap; §17).
rationale: Adds the pushes that the boss chapters already make.

old: The attack of a push-move with a damage value is defended as any other enemy attack (see §9.4; §9.5).
new: The attack of a push-move with a damage value is defended by a block or a dodge, as any other enemy attack is (see §9.4; §9.5). No *parry* of it is permitted (see §9.6).
rationale: §8.4 read as if a parry were allowed; §9.2 and §9.6 forbid it.

old: Each condition lasts until the rule under its heading removes it. Where a token is removed at the end of a model's next complete *turn*, a token placed
new: Each condition lasts until the rule under its heading removes it. The end of the affected model's own *turn* is the only moment at which a turn acts on a condition: poison is then resolved, and frostbite and stagger tokens are then removed. Where a token is removed at the end of a model's next complete turn, a token placed
rationale: States the one clock that poison, frostbite and stagger share, which step 3 of the character turn relies on.
evidence: Official 2017 and 2022 resolve all three at the end of the model's own activation (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 968-971, 986-988; DS-TG 1483-1512).

old: A value reduced by a condition cannot fall below zero.
new: A value reduced by a condition cannot fall below zero. When the *aggro token* is assigned, bleed damage counts as damage inflicted by the character whose attack triggered it, and poison damage counts for no character (see §7.5, Encounter Turn Order; §16.4).
rationale: Settles which condition damage counts towards the aggro token without any new book-keeping.
evidence: No source addresses it; follows from when the damage is recorded.

old: An icon that has no valid *target*, or that cannot be resolved, is skipped, and the next icon to the right is resolved. The enemy's turn ends when its last icon has been resolved or when the enemy is killed.
new: An icon that has no valid *target*, or that cannot be resolved, is skipped, and the next icon to the right is resolved. If the data card bears the *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}}, the enemy resolves its whole row of icons the number of times shown, and the target of each icon is determined again each time. The enemy's turn ends when its last icon has been resolved for the last time or when the enemy is killed.
rationale: States the repeat rule for an enemy data card where the row of icons is described, in the words §16.1 uses for a boss.

old:
- A *condition* icon places the matching condition token on each character hit by the attack (see §8.5).
- A *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} causes the attack to be resolved the number of times shown, and the target is determined afresh each time. A repeat icon applies only to the attack icon beside it, not to a movement icon.
new:
- A *condition* icon places the matching condition token on each character hit by the attack (see §8.5).

A *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} on the data card repeats the enemy's whole row of icons, not one attack (see §9.1).
rationale: Deletes the attack-only special case, which was written for the scaling rule that Gate 1 removed.

old:
### Defence

When an attack targets a character, the character's player must choose one defence before any dice are rolled.
new:
### Attack Sequence

An enemy attack is resolved as follows.

1. Determine the target (see §9.3, Targets).
2. Check the range. If the target is not within range, skip the icon.
3. Choose the character's defence (see §9.3, Defence).
4. Resolve the defence (see §9.4; §9.5; §9.6). If a dodge or a parry succeeds, the character is not hit, and the attack on that character ends.
5. Place the damage that the defence has not prevented (see §3.4).
6. If the attack is a push-attack, push the character (see §8.4).
7. Place any condition token the attack carries (see §8.5).

Steps 6 and 7 are resolved even if the character suffered no damage. A character who dies in step 5 is not pushed and receives no token. A node attack resolves steps 3 to 7 for one character at a time, in an order chosen by the players. The attack of a push-move with a damage value follows the same steps from step 3 (see §8.4).

### Defence

When an attack targets a character, the character's player must choose one defence before any dice are rolled.
rationale: States the order of an enemy attack once, as §10.3 does for a character attack, so that §8.4, §8.5, §9.4, §9.5, §9.6 and §16.3 have one sequence to match.
evidence: Official 2022 numbered attack steps (DS-TG 1667-1763); this book, §8.4 and §8.5 (damage, then push, then condition).

old: 7. Place any *condition* token the attack carries (see §8.5) and resolve any *push* (see §8.4), even if the character suffered no damage.
new: 7. Resolve any *push* (see §8.4), then place any *condition* token the attack carries (see §8.5), even if the character suffered no damage.
rationale: Step 7 gave the condition before the push; §8.5 and §10.3 give the push first, and the order decides whether a stagger token affects the dodge of a trap entered by the push.
evidence: This book, §8.5 second paragraph and §10.3 step 11.

old: - A *shield* is equipped in the character's left *weapon slot* (see §3.2; §4.1).
new: - A *shield* is equipped in one of the character's *weapon slots* (see §3.2; §4.1).
rationale: The parry was the only rule in the book that depended on which weapon slot held a card; the choice of slot carried no decision.
evidence: Audit finding A-068 (approved, REQUIRED) proposed the same; no official or community ruleset has a left-hand rule.

old: A shield in the right weapon slot does not permit a parry. A character who wields
new: The shield may be in either weapon slot. A character who wields
rationale: As combat-E22.

old: A riposte is one attack against the attacker, made with one *attack option* of the *weapon* equipped in the character's right weapon slot.
new: A riposte is one attack against the attacker, made with one *attack option* of the *weapon* equipped in the character's other weapon slot, the slot that does not hold the shield used for the parry. A *spell* cannot be used for a riposte, whether it is equipped in that slot or stored in a *catalyst* there (see §4.3).
rationale: Follows the either-slot parry and states the spell exclusion that the word "weapon" only implied.

old: No riposte is made if the right weapon slot holds no weapon with an attack option,
new: No riposte is made if the other weapon slot holds no weapon with an attack option,
rationale: As combat-E22.

old: Range is checked when the target is chosen, after any shift resolved before the dice. A character cannot make an attack that has no permitted target within its range.
new: Range is checked when the target is chosen, after any shift resolved before the dice. A character cannot begin an attack unless a permitted target is within its range or a shift printed before its dice is able to bring one within range. If no permitted target is within range when the target is to be chosen, the attack ends without a roll, and the stamina paid is not returned.
rationale: Step 4 had no outcome when a shift, or a trap entered during it, left no target in range.
evidence: Official 2022 pays and shifts before the target is chosen (DS-TG 1421-1423, 1546-1549); no source gives the outcome.

old: An attack option that bears the *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} is resolved in full the number of times shown in the icon. The character pays the stamina cost once, before the first resolution, and then resolves steps 3 to 12 of the attack once for each time shown.
new: An attack option that bears the *repeat* icon {{icon:ast-0061-repeat-behaviour-or-attack}} may be resolved in full up to the number of times shown in the icon. The character pays the stamina cost once, before the first resolution, resolves steps 3 to 12 of the attack for each resolution, and may stop after any resolution.
rationale: A repeated attack is a permission, as every other attack of the Attack major action is ("up to one attack with each weapon").
evidence: Official 2022: "perform the attack up to the number of times shown" (DS-TG 1566-1572).

old: A spell card equipped while the other weapon slot is empty gains no reroll, and the attack options of a spell stored in a catalyst gain none.
new: A spell card equipped while the other weapon slot is empty gains no reroll, and the attack options of a spell stored in a catalyst gain none. A catalyst is a weapon: an attack option printed on the catalyst card itself gains the reroll while the catalyst is wielded two-handed.
rationale: Applies the general rule to the one card type the section left open; no special case is created.
evidence: This book, §4.1 (a catalyst is a weapon) and §10.4.

old: *Spells* are never scaled (see §4.3).
new: A weapon whose four stat requirements are all zero has no relevant stat and is never scaled. *Spells* are never scaled (see §4.3).
rationale: Without it every character scales such a weapon at once, a +1 that rewards nothing and a red cube that records no choice.
evidence: Audit finding A-066; no official or community ruleset has stat scaling.

old: Which weapon slot holds a shield matters for the *parry* and the *riposte* (see §9.6).
new: A shield in either weapon slot permits a *parry*, and the *riposte* is made with the weapon in the other weapon slot (see §9.6).
rationale: Follows §9.6 as changed by combat-E22.

old: the model with the most *wound tokens* takes its turn first.
new: the model whose *wound tokens* have the greatest total value takes its turn first.
rationale: Wound tokens have values of 1, 3 and 5, so their number is not the damage.

old: counting wound tokens placed and damage recorded on an invader's health dial.
new: counting the total value of the wound tokens placed and the damage recorded on an invader's health dial.
rationale: As combat-E31.

old:
- The defender may *parry* as against an enemy's attack, with the attacker in the place of the enemy, if the conditions for a parry are met (see §9.6). The dodge difficulty is given by the same table.
- The defender may decline to defend. The defender suffers damage equal to the attack value and is hit.
new: - The defender may *parry* as against an enemy's attack, with the attacker in the place of the enemy, if the conditions for a parry are met (see §9.6). The dodge difficulty is given by the same table.
rationale: A block or resist costs nothing and is never worse than no defence, so the fourth option was dead text and disagreed with the three defences of §9.3.

old: **A.** No. A parry requires a shield in the left weapon slot. A weapon that bears
new: **A.** No. A parry requires a shield in a weapon slot. A weapon that bears
rationale: Follows §9.6 as changed by combat-E22.

old: Each of its attack options then adds one to its attack value. Spells are never scaled (see §10.5).
new: Each of its attack options then adds one to its attack value. A weapon whose stat requirements are all zero is never scaled, and spells are never scaled (see §10.5).
rationale: Follows §10.5 as changed by combat-E29.

old: **Repeat.** An icon that causes an entire attack option or behaviour card to be resolved the number of times shown. For a character's attack option the stamina cost is paid once and each resolution is a separate attack roll with its own target (see §10.3, Repeat).
new: **Repeat.** An icon that causes an entire attack option, or the whole row of behaviour icons on an enemy data card or a behaviour card, to be resolved more than once. A character may resolve the attack option up to the number of times shown: the stamina cost is paid once, and each resolution is a separate attack roll with its own target (see §10.3, Repeat). An enemy or a boss resolves its row of icons the number of times shown (see §9.1; §16.1).
rationale: Glossary follows §9.1, §10.3 and §16.1.

old: **Push.** Forced movement of a model from its node to an adjacent valid node. A push is caused by a push-attack, by a push-move, by the node model limit, or by a boss model moving onto the node of another boss model. A push is not a move and costs no stamina; a gravestone, a chest, and a pillar token block it, and a push with no valid node does not happen (see §8.4).
new: **Push.** Forced movement of a model from its node to an adjacent valid node. A push is caused by a push-attack, by a push-move, by the node model limit, by a boss model moving onto the node of another boss model, or by a rule of a boss such as a leap. A push is not a move and costs no stamina; a gravestone, a chest, and a pillar token block it, and a push with no valid node does not happen (see §8.4).
rationale: Glossary follows §8.4.

old: **Condition.** A lasting effect marked by a condition token on a model: *bleed*, *poison*, *frostbite*, *stagger*, *calamity*, or *corrosion*. A condition token is placed on each model hit by an attack that bears the matching icon, after the attack is resolved. A model holds at most one token of each condition, except poison (see §8.5).
new: **Condition.** A lasting effect marked by a condition token on a model: *bleed*, *poison*, *frostbite*, *stagger*, *calamity*, or *corrosion*. A condition token is placed on each model hit by an attack that bears the matching icon, after the attack's damage and any push have been resolved. A model holds at most one token of each condition, except poison (see §8.5).
rationale: Glossary states the same order as §8.5 and the attack sequence.

old: **Parry.** A defence available to a character with a shield equipped in the left weapon slot when the attacker is on the character's node; an attack that pushes, a node attack, and a boss attack outside §15.6 cannot be parried. The character pays one stamina and rolls dodge dice against the attack's dodge difficulty. Success makes the attack miss, staggers the attacker, and allows a *riposte*; failure deals the full attack value with no block or resist roll and staggers the character (see §9.6).
new: **Parry.** A defence available to a character with a shield equipped in either weapon slot when the attacker is on the character's node; an attack that pushes, a node attack, and a boss attack outside §15.6 cannot be parried. The character pays one stamina and rolls dodge dice against the attack's dodge difficulty. Success makes the attack miss, staggers the attacker, and allows a *riposte*; failure deals the full attack value with no block or resist roll and staggers the character (see §9.6).
rationale: Glossary follows §9.6.

old: **Riposte.** The attack a character may make at once against the attacker after a successful *parry*, using one attack option of the weapon in the right weapon slot and paying its stamina cost. A riposte cannot be parried, and it does not count against the attacks of the character's own turn (see §9.6).
new: **Riposte.** The attack a character may make at once against the attacker after a successful *parry*, using one attack option of the weapon in the other weapon slot, never a spell, and paying its stamina cost. A riposte cannot be parried, and it does not count against the attacks of the character's own turn (see §9.6).
rationale: Glossary follows §9.6.

old: **Scaled (weapon).** A weapon equipped by a character whose *relevant stat* exceeds the weapon's highest printed stat requirement by five or more. It is marked with a red cube and each of its attack options adds one to its attack value. Spells are never scaled (see §10.5).
new: **Scaled (weapon).** A weapon equipped by a character whose *relevant stat* exceeds the weapon's highest printed stat requirement by five or more. It is marked with a red cube and each of its attack options adds one to its attack value. A weapon whose stat requirements are all zero is never scaled, and spells are never scaled (see §10.5).
rationale: Glossary follows §10.5.

old: **Attack value.** The total of the values rolled on an attack's dice after rerolls, with any fixed modifier applied once to the total, plus one for a *scaled* weapon and minus one for a *staggered* attacker, to a minimum of zero (see §10.3). For enemies the attack value is the fixed number printed in the attack icon, scaled for the number of characters (see §9.3).
new: **Attack value.** The total of the values rolled on an attack's dice after rerolls, with any fixed modifier applied once to the total, plus one for a *scaled* weapon and minus one for a *staggered* attacker, to a minimum of zero (see §10.3). For enemies the attack value is the fixed number printed in the attack icon, or the damage value of a push-move, scaled for the number of characters and reduced by one while the enemy is *staggered* (see §8.3; §8.4; §9.3).
rationale: Adds the push-move damage value and the stagger reduction, which §8.3, §8.4 and §8.5 already treat as part of an enemy attack value.

old: **Magical damage.** Damage from an attack marked with the white circle icon. Magical damage is reduced by resist.
new: **Magical damage.** Damage from an attack that bears the magical damage icon. Magical damage is reduced by resist (see §9.3; §10.3).
rationale: Names the icon as §4.3, §8.2, §9.3 and §10.3 name it.

old: **Physical damage.** Damage from an attack marked with the crossed swords icon. Physical damage is reduced by block.
new: **Physical damage.** Damage from an enemy attack marked with the crossed swords icon, or from a character's attack option that does not bear the magical damage icon. Physical damage is reduced by block (see §9.3; §10.3).
rationale: A character's attack option shows no crossed swords icon; it deals physical damage by default (§10.3).
